# Local bring-up

This page is the operator-first path for starting CALIBER locally and verifying
that the runtime is healthy before you use deeper feature or architecture docs.

## At a glance

| Path | Use when | Entry point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full suite | You want the complete local stack around CALIBER | `make setup`, `make start` |
| Standalone dev | You want the shortest supported CALIBER edit/test loop inside `caliber/` | `docker compose ... --profile app up -d mlflow`, then `caliber-migrate`, then `uvicorn caliber.server:create_app --factory --reload --port 5001` |
| Readiness check | You want to confirm dependency posture after boot | `GET /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/readiness` |
| Recovery path | You need failure handling, not first boot | [Operations runbook](m-19-runbook.md) |

## 1. Full suite path

Use the full suite when you want the local product as it is usually demonstrated:
CALIBER, MLflow, storage, and the surrounding services together.

```bash
make setup
make start
```

`make start` runs `./start.sh`, which brings up the Compose `app` profile and the NATS bus:
MinIO (with its buckets created), PostgreSQL with pgvector and Apache AGE, MLflow on `:5000`, the
MLflow AI Gateway on `:5002` and CALIBER on `:5001`. Every published port is bound to `127.0.0.1`.
The CALIBER container runs `alembic upgrade head` before it serves, so this path needs no manual
migration. It seeds `admin` / `admin` on the first boot only, for loopback use.
`./start.sh` rebuilds the images and recreates the app containers by default; `make start CLEAN_START=0 BUILD=0`
reuses them.

Then verify:

- CALIBER UI loads at `http://localhost:5001/caliber/`
- login succeeds
- readiness reports a usable local posture. The stack sets the LLM provider to `fake`, so expect
  `llm` under `simulated`; the evaluator, promoter and artifact store are `mlflow`.
- the gateway is serving. With no `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the suite-root `.env`
  the `mlflow-gateway` container exits and Compose restarts it in a loop, and the Gateway page reports
  it unreachable ([Operator troubleshooting](m-51-operator-troubleshooting.md#3-the-gateway-reports-unreachable)).
  CALIBER itself does not depend on it.

The stack starts with the preview areas **off**: Aria and plans, MCP servers, OpenAPI integrations, cookbooks, and
release-candidate signoff are off by default, so their navigation entries are hidden. To try one, set the variable in
the suite-root `.env` (`.env.example` documents them) and run `make start` again; see
[Preview areas](#preview-areas-are-off-by-default) below.

To prove a fresh clone does all of this, `scripts/verify-compose-stack.sh` builds the CALIBER and MLflow
images, starts the stack from the example environment as its own Compose project
(`caliber-stack-smoke`) and checks MLflow, `/health`, `/readiness`, the SPA, login, a project and a
prompt. `.github/workflows/stack-smoke.yml` runs it weekly, on manual dispatch and on pull requests
that change `deploy/`. It is not a required check.

## 2. Standalone development path

Use the standalone path when you are developing CALIBER itself and want the
shorter supported inner loop. Start vanilla MLflow and its dependencies from the
repository root without starting the containerized CALIBER service:

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile app up -d mlflow

cd caliber
make install
export CALIBER_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://caliber:caliber@127.0.0.1:5432/caliber
caliber-migrate   # creates or upgrades the tables; the server never does
export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://127.0.0.1:5000
export CALIBER_ADMIN_USERS=admin CALIBER_OPERATOR_USERS=admin CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS=admin
export CALIBER_AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false
export CALIBER_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEFAULT=true
uvicorn caliber.server:create_app --factory --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5001
```

Optional frontend dev loop:

```bash
cd caliber/caliber-ui
npm install
npm run dev
```

`caliber-migrate` must run before the first start and after upgrades; the server never creates
its own tables. The role variables decide what the first login may do. For an install from wheels
with no checkout, use [Alpha install](m-60-alpha-install.md).

Vite proxies API calls to the standalone CALIBER process on `:5001` by default.
The insecure bootstrap flags are for trusted loopback use only; change the
first-boot password immediately and never use them for a network-reachable deployment.

## 3. Health and readiness

After either path, do not assume the runtime is usable just because the process
started.

Verify both:

- liveness: `/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/health`
- readiness: `/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/readiness`

The readiness endpoint is the meaningful one for operator decisions.

Then move to:

- [Health and readiness](m-50-health-and-readiness.md)
- [Configuration and provider setup](m-48-configuration-and-provider-setup.md)

## Preview areas are off by default

Four server-side flags keep the areas the alpha does not stand behind switched off, on both paths above:

| Variable | Turns on |
| --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_ARIA` | The Aria assistant and plans |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS` | MCP servers and OpenAPI integrations |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_COOKBOOKS` | Cookbooks |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES` | Release-candidate signoff and Workspace releases |

Set the variable to `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on`, and restart CALIBER, because the flags are read once at startup.
In the full suite, put them in the suite-root `.env`; Compose passes them through to the CALIBER container, and
they default to false. For the standalone path, export them before `uvicorn`. Confirm with `features` in
`GET /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/capabilities`. Enabling a flag means you accept that area's preview behavior;
see [Feature flags](m-61-alpha-scope.md#feature-flags).

## 4. First local login

The local bootstrap path is only for loopback bring-up. Rotate any insecure
bootstrap defaults before exposing the deployment beyond the local machine.

For the deeper trust boundary and scope model, use:

- [Platform](m-01-platform.md)
- [Operations runbook](m-19-runbook.md)
